title: All-Inclusive Holidays in Bol, Brač: Guide 2027
metaDescription: Bol has real all-inclusive options: Bretanide and Bluesun Bonaca. Prices per person, what is included, and who should choose all-inclusive or an apartment.
content:
## Are there all-inclusive hotels in Bol?

Yes. Bol has a small number of real all-inclusive hotels, all on the Zlatni Rat side of town along the seafront promenade.

- **Bretanide Sport & Wellness Resort (4*)** is the clearest all-inclusive resort in Bol. It markets itself as an all-inclusive sport and wellness resort, with a pebble beach, pools and spa.
- **Bluesun Holiday Village Bonaca (3*)** is the budget family option. It sits in pine forest above Hotel Borak, about 150 m from the sea, and is sold as a family all-inclusive hotel with free places for two children under 14 in the family offer.

The other large Bluesun hotels, Borak and Elaphusa, are mainly sold as bed and breakfast or half board. Confirm the meal plan when booking, because availability changes by year and by agency.

Bol is not an all-inclusive destination in the Turkish or Spanish sense. Most of the town is made up of small family hotels, guesthouses and apartments, and the old harbour has dozens of konobas. That is why the all-inclusive stock is so small.

## What is usually included

At Bol's all-inclusive hotels the package typically covers:

- Buffet breakfast (Bonaca: 7:00–10:00), with a late continental breakfast until midday
- Buffet lunch with show cooking (Bonaca: 12:30–14:30)
- Afternoon coffee and cake (Bonaca: 16:00–17:30)
- Buffet dinner (Bonaca: 18:30–21:30)
- Local house drinks with meals and at the bar during set hours
- Pool use and, depending on the hotel, parts of the sports programme

Spa and wellness entry, premium drinks, tennis and bowling are normally charged extra. At the Bluesun hotels, wellness is not included in the room rate, and parking costs about €9–11 per day. Tourist tax is small, around €1 per person per night in some rate sheets.

## Price per person per night: all-inclusive vs half-board vs apartment

### Peak season (mid-July to mid-August)

- **All-inclusive:** about €110–150 per person at the resorts. A 7-night all-inclusive week at Bretanide has been offered at about €800 per person in the late-June to mid-July window, with higher rates in the middle of the season.
- **Half board:** Bluesun Hotel Borak lists about €161–186 per person per night in July and August, depending on the room.
- **Private apartment:** about €80–150 per night for a two-person unit, or €40–75 per person. Add €20–30 per person per day for groceries and a few restaurant meals.

### Shoulder season (late May–June, September)

- **All-inclusive:** about €60–95 per person. Bretanide has advertised eight-day all-inclusive packages from around €750 per person.
- **Half board:** Borak lists about €91–137 per person in late May and early June, and €69–74 for the last days of September.
- **Private apartment:** about €50–90 per night for two, or €25–45 per person, before food.

In the low season, Borak's bed and breakfast price is about €48 per person per night, and the half-board supplement is about €10–21 per person depending on the season.

These are rough ranges based on current published rates. Dynamic pricing and tour-operator packages can move them considerably.

## Who all-inclusive suits in Bol

**Families with small children.** This is the best match. Fixed meal times, buffets that handle fussy eaters, pools, and a short walk to a shallow pebble beach all simplify the day. Bonaca's free-child-place offer makes it the cheapest way to feed a family of four. The promenade from Zlatni Rat to the town centre is flat and takes about 25–30 minutes on foot, so a pushchair works.

**Short stays of 3–5 nights.** Shopping, cooking and checking apartment key logistics is not worth it for a brief stay. A package also removes the need to find restaurants that book up in July.

**Active guests.** Those who want tennis, windsurfing or spa time on site can use an all-inclusive resort as a base. Some of this is charged separately at the Bluesun properties, so check what is bundled.

## Who is better off self-catering

- **Couples and groups of adults.** Bol's konobas and fish restaurants are the reason to be here. A grilled fish dinner with wine costs about €30–45 per person, but it is better than a hotel buffet.
- **Stays of 7 nights or longer in peak season.** A private apartment, with a market shop at the local grocery and a few restaurant dinners, usually costs about half the all-inclusive rate.
- **Windsurfers and kitesurfers.** Wind peaks in the afternoon, which clashes with fixed lunch hours.
- **Day-trippers.** Anyone planning to spend days at Vidova Gora, Blaca Hermitage or on ferry trips will pay for meals they do not eat.

One firm opinion: an all-inclusive week in Bol in July or August is poor value for adults without small children. Half board at Borak costs more than a full all-inclusive board at the resort, and neither beats an apartment plus a few dinners out in the old town.

## Local tips

- Book the all-inclusive rate directly or through the hotel's own site. Bluesun states that its website and reservation centre prices are the same.
- Zlatni Rat is about 1.5–2 km west of the harbour. The promenade is shaded by pines, and the hotels at the Zlatni Rat end are the closest to it.
- Late September gives the best balance. The sea is still warm, and half-board prices at Borak drop to about €69–74 per person in the final days.
- Reach Bol by catamaran or ferry from Split to Supetar, then a bus or taxi, or by catamaran direct to Bol in summer. Brač airport is also an option for seasonal flights.
- Check how drinks are handled. At Bluesun half board, only breakfast hot drinks, juice and water are included, and everything else is charged according to the price list.

## Nearest all-inclusive alternatives

All-inclusive stock on Brač beyond Bol is limited, so Bol itself is the island's main base for it. For a wider choice, travellers usually look at larger resort towns on the mainland Makarska Riviera, reachable by ferry from the island, for example via Sumartin–Makarska or Split.

faq.question: Does Bol have all-inclusive hotels?
faq.answer: Yes. Bretanide Sport & Wellness Resort (4*) sells all-inclusive, and Bluesun Holiday Village Bonaca (3*) is marketed as a family all-inclusive hotel. Other Bol hotels, such as Borak and Elaphusa, are mainly sold on a bed and breakfast or half-board basis.

faq.question: How much does all-inclusive cost in Bol per person per night?
faq.answer: Roughly €95–150 per person per night in peak summer and about €60–95 in shoulder season. Bretanide has quoted about €800 per person for 7 nights in the late June to mid-July window.

faq.question: Is all-inclusive cheaper than half-board in Bol?
faq.answer: It can be. Half board at Hotel Borak lists about €161–186 per person in July and August, which is more than the all-inclusive rates quoted at the resorts. The cheapest option is Bonaca, where all-inclusive room rates start around €40 per person in low season.

faq.question: What is not included in all-inclusive in Bol?
faq.answer: Spa and wellness entry, premium drinks, tennis, bowling and parking are usually extra. Parking at the Bluesun hotels is around €9–11 per day.

faq.question: Is a private apartment cheaper than all-inclusive in Bol?
faq.answer: Usually, yes, for stays of a week or more and for adults. An apartment costs about €25–75 per person per night, plus €20–30 per day for food. For families with small children and short stays, all-inclusive is often easier and similar in cost.
